quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
rationale: Section 10(a) gives us an express Kubient duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless AP and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees against all third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors. Read with the §9(b) warranties, that reaches third-party IP infringement (9(b)(i): the Service and deliverables "do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party"), Vendor-caused data/security failures (9(b)(iii)), and Kubient's breach of applicable Law (9(b)(ix)), with negligence and wilful misconduct captured by the "acts or omissions of Kubient" limb. Section 11 supplies the full standard procedure: prompt written notice (without forfeiture for delay), indemnitor control of defence and settlement subject to our consent for any settlement admitting our liability, and reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost. The clause therefore sits at or above the fallback and substantially meets the preferred position, and it is materially better than fallback in two respects that favour us: there are no Customer-modification/combination/specification exclusions, and Kubient's indemnity is not subject to any super-cap (§7(a) also carves indemnification out of the damages exclusion). We note three sub-preferred points for the record rather than redlining them: "affiliates" are not named as indemnified parties (officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees are); there is no procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder; and AP's reciprocal §10(b) indemnity is broader than the preferred "Customer content and Customer's breach of law," extending to unauthorized use of the Services/Platform and AP's acts or omissions. None of these is a walk-away or a material fallback failure, and proposing the fallback's 3x annual-fee super-cap would weaken our current uncapped recourse, so we do not redline.

verification.notes: The finding of 'missing' is sound: the Agreement has no IP/data-ownership article, and the only grant to Customer (paragraph 2) is limited, non-sublicensable and revocable, which fails the fallback on material terms. Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted paragraph delivers Vendor retention of generic tools/know-how, and a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables for Customer's business, plus a solely-to-provide-the-Services limit on any Kubient licence in Customer data. Preferred is not complete: there is no Customer ownership of or assignment of Deliverables, no affirmative 'Customer retains all rights in Customer Data' sentence, and no express bar on joint ownership. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add (i) 'Kubient hereby assigns to Customer all right, title and interest in the deliverables and work product created for Customer', (ii) 'Customer retains all right, title and interest in Customer Data', and (iii) 'No intellectual property will be jointly owned.' The words 'and the Auction Platform' in the retention sentence lightly overlap with warranty (viii) but serve as the anchor for that carve-out. Preserves intent: paragraph 2's Auction Platform licence, paragraph 25(a)'s use restrictions on the Service, and the Kubient warranties survive without contradiction, and no new assignment exception or Vendor-favourable transfer right is created. Drafting caution to verify before sending: confirm 'Requests' is a defined term in the Agreement; if it is not, drop the capitalisation or delete it, since the catch-all 'any other data or materials belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer' already carries the element and an undefined capitalised term risks a dangling reference.

quote: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION, OR LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES
rationale: Section 7 (Limitation of Liability) contains only a mutual exclusion of consequential/indirect damages (with indemnification and confidentiality carved out of that exclusion). Nothing in Section 7, the warranty section (Section 9), the indemnity sections (Sections 10-11) or the general provisions imposes any aggregate liability cap, so both parties' direct liability is unlimited and the fallback element "cap based on 12 months of fees" fails outright. We therefore add a single mutual cap sentence. Because the commercial structure is a revenue share (Section 5) under which Customer pays no material fees, a bare 12-months'-fees cap would be illusory; we target the preferred position so the USD 1,000,000 floor applies, and keep indemnification, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP outside the cap, with Customer's payment obligations not treated as capped damages. The existing mutual consequential-damages exclusion already satisfies that preferred element and is left untouched.

rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on AP. Section 1 (p0001) affirmatively disclaims any exclusive arrangement and confirms AP remains free to offer Inventory through other agents or sell it directly to third parties, which satisfies the preferred position. I checked every other candidate: the "exclusive" references at p0002 (non-exclusive licence to AP), p0064 (exclusive forum), p0065 (each Party's own marks), p0072 (entire agreement) and p0073 (no third-party beneficiaries) are unrelated to exclusive dealing, and no requirements-purchase, sole-source, right-of-first-refusal or "shall not procure from any third party" language appears. Section 5 (p0023) makes Kubient responsible, absent contrary Exhibit terms, for contracting with all Advertisers on AP's behalf, but that is a default allocation of Kubient's own duties, is overridable in an Exhibit, and is expressly subject to AP's retained freedom in Section 1, so it does not create exclusivity. quote: Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement,
rationale: Nothing in the Agreement imposes liquidated damages, penalties, an early-termination fee or a minimum fee payable by AP. Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty" and "termination fee" return nothing, and the only money mechanics are (i) the revenue-share in section 5, under which value flows from Kubient to AP ("payment from Kubient to Customer shall be made within seven (7) days from Kubient's receipt of payment"), and (ii) the quoted sentence in section 4(a), which merely preserves Kubient's share of fees actually generated during the 90-day notice period while Services continue — it is a pro-rata entitlement to earned revenue, not a pre-agreed sum payable by AP on termination. Section 7 also excludes punitive and special damages for both Parties. The Agreement therefore meets the preferred position (Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties), so the fallback early-termination-fee cap is not engaged and no redline is warranted.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition not engaged: the renewal clause permits no price increase on renewal, so no 5% cap language is needed and its absence is not a gap.

verification.notes: Fallback is complete: the single inserted phrase creates the missing Customer non-renewal right at exactly 60 days, and the price-cap element is not triggered because paragraph 4(a) contains no renewal uplift mechanic. Preferred is not reached: the opt-out is 60 rather than 30 days and there is no Vendor obligation to remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal. To move to preferred, replace "sixty (60)" with "thirty (30)" and add an express Kubient reminder obligation not less than sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current Term. Minimality holds: the edit adds only the operative words needed for the fallback element and deletes nothing. Vendor's separate 90-day post-Initial-Term convenience right, the material-breach mechanics, and the "Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period" allocation are all retained untouched, and the drafter correctly declined to touch the T4C notice period under this rule. Intent preserved: the insertion sits inside the existing "unless" construction without breaking the "Term" definition parenthetical, creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and non-renewal at natural term end does not contradict the retained sentence barring termination during the Initial Term (non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as a mid-term termination). If the drafter wants to remove any residual argument that a non-renewal notice served during the Initial Term is a prohibited "termination during the Initial Term," adding "effective at the end of the then-current Term" would be a clarifying, not required, tweak. Finding status "deviation" is correct: before the edit the only exit was a 90-day convenience notice, so Customer had no non-renewal window at or under the 60-day fallback ceiling.

mappings.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4(c) only stops the Services and addresses Confidential Information, so we have no exit help and no right to get our data back. We have added a short clause at our fallback position: at least 90 days of transition assistance and export of our data within 30 days after expiry or termination.

ops.text: Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Kubient shall (i) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiry or termination; and (ii) within thirty (30) days following such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Customer all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer that is then in Kubient's possession or control.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data export obligations on expiry or termination

rationale: The only effect-of-termination provision (Section 4(c), p0019–p0022) requires Kubient to cease the Services, revokes the licence, and obliges each Party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information. There is no transition assistance obligation and no obligation to export or return Customer's data (Requests, revenue/auction data or other data processed for AP) in any timeframe, and nothing elsewhere in the Agreement supplies it. The rule therefore fails at the fallback, so we insert a short clause at the fallback level: at least 90 days of transition assistance on expiry or termination and export of AP data within 30 days of expiry or termination. We have not volunteered the preferred six-month/machine-readable/certified-deletion package.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause opens "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Kubient shall...", and both limbs are anchored to "following such expiry or termination".

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Inserted limb (i) provides "reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days"; no six-month period appears anywhere. To reach preferred, change to "up to six (6) months".

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: The inserted assistance limb is silent on pricing; no "then-current rates" language was added and none exists in Section 4(c).

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (ii): "within thirty (30) days following such expiry or termination, export and deliver to Customer all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer that is then in Kubient's possession or control."

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Limb (ii) specifies no format; "commonly used, machine-readable format" wording was deliberately not included.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion-and-certification limb was inserted; retained Section 4(c)(iv) only requires each Party to "return or destroy" Confidential Information, with no written certification and no sequencing after return.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: "Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Kubient shall..." — covers every covered exit event, and both obligations run from that event rather than from an anticipated expiry.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Limb (i): "at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for a period of at least ninety (90) days following such expiry or termination" — floor of 90 days, running post-termination.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Limb (ii) requires export and delivery "within thirty (30) days following such expiry or termination" of "all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Customer", i.e. the full Customer data category, not selected named types.

verification.notes: Fallback checklist is fully met by the single inserted paragraph: exit trigger on expiry or termination for any reason, a 90-day floor of transition assistance, and export of all Customer data within 30 days of that event. Preferred is incomplete on four elements — six-month duration, then-current rates, machine-readable format, and post-return certified deletion. The drafter correctly declined to volunteer them; to escalate later, amend limb (i) to "up to six (6) months at Kubient's then-current rates", add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to limb (ii), and add a limb (iii) requiring deletion and written certification thereafter. Minimal: nothing in existing Section 4(c) was deleted or reworded, the insertion carries no survival tail, expense allocation, remedy or procedural boilerplate, and the "at Customer's request" condition is a general request mechanic (not one tied only to anticipated expiry), so it does not undercut the trigger. Intent preserved: cessation of Services, licence revocation, Customer's cease-use obligation and the mutual Confidential Information return/destroy mechanic all survive; the new specific export duty overlays, and does not contradict, the general return-or-destroy option, and no undefined terms or dangling cross-references are introduced. Comment is accurate, concise and cites the fallback position without overclaiming; classification as a missing-clause insert is correct because no transition or data-return obligation existed anywhere.

mappings.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
Warranty remedies include a refund.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Kubient warranties contain no conformance-to-documentation commitment and no warranty remedy, so we have added our fallback position: 90 days for the Service and deliverables, 30 days for services, with repair, replacement or refund of fees paid.

ops.text: for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, the Service, the Auction Platform and any deliverables provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to their documentation, and for a period of thirty (30) days following performance, the services provided hereunder will conform in all material respects to the requirements of this Agreement. Customer's remedy for breach of this clause (xii) is, at Kubient's option, repair or replacement of the non-conforming item or a refund of the fees paid for it.

proposal.summary: Add 90-day software/deliverable documentation conformance warranty, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replace or refund remedy.

quote: (ii) the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards;
rationale: Kubient gives several express warranties (industry-standard performance, no malicious code, compliance with Laws, freedom from utility-affecting errors), and the disclaimer in Section 13 expressly preserves them, so the "as is" language does not swallow the express warranties. However, the Agreement contains no warranty that the Service, Auction Platform or deliverables will conform to their documentation for any period and, critically, no warranty remedy at all — no repair, replacement or refund. That fails the fallback on two material terms (documentation conformance for at least 90 days for software, at least 30 days for services, plus repair/replace and refund remedies). We therefore propose the shortest fallback-level insertion adding the conformance periods and the repair/replacement-or-refund remedy; the preferred 12-month software period and "professional and workmanlike" formulation are noted as our upgrade ask only.

verification.notes: The fallback checklist is complete: 90-day documentation conformance for the Service/Auction Platform/deliverables, a 30-day services warranty, and a repair-or-replacement-or-refund remedy are all in the inserted operative text. Preferred is not reached: no "professional and workmanlike manner" standard, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, and the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days. The no-malicious-code element could not be verified from the paragraphs supplied \u2014 if it is not actually present elsewhere in Section (b), the preferred gap is wider than the comment suggests. Minimality holds: the insertion is a single new sub-clause supplying only the missing conformance periods and remedy; nothing favourable is deleted, the existing warranties (ii), (vi), (ix)\u2013(xi) survive untouched, and the Section 13 disclaimer\u2019s "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement" carve-out already preserves the new express warranty, so no disclaimer edit was needed. Intent is preserved: the 30-day services conformance warranty sits alongside, and does not contradict, retained clause (vi) (which is unlimited in time as to compliance with the Agreement and utility-affecting errors); the new clause adds a remedy rather than displacing existing rights. Drafting repair to make before sending: the remedy sentence refers to "this clause (xii)" but the inserted paragraph as rendered carries no (xii) enumerator following clause (xi). Add the "(xii)" designator (or change the reference to "this clause") so the cross-reference is not dangling. Optional upgrade ask, consistent with the comment: seek 12 months for the Auction Platform/Service and a "professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards" performance warranty, but the current text is already acceptable at the fallback.
